messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT /pager — Latency SLO breach detected for hosted inference (p99 > SLO). Auto-page sent to #eng-oncall.

alex: paging: saw p95 jump ~120ms -> ~920ms and p99 spikes to ~3.1s at ~17:02 UTC. Streaming stalls up to 40% of streams. Many requests stuck during decode phase. @maria you on call?

maria: I'm on. seeing the alert, jumping in. any customer-facing incidents tied to this yet?

support-pager: FYI: 3 high-usage customers reported increased end-to-end latency in support tickets, ticket ids: #5432, #5437, #5440. All using streaming endpoints and long-turn prompts.

sam: adding logs: tail of worker logs shows repeated cache-miss cascades and eviction churn. snippets:```WARN kv_cache: shard=7 evict=1200 miss_rate=0.78 prefills=0.62```

jess: where are the prefill vs decode durations trending? I want to know if prefill is preempting decode and causing cache thrash.

alex: timeline: spike started after a small rollout (traffic-split change) 10m before alerts. We routed more traffic to v2-serving pool which has new prefill heuristic enabled. Could be related.

maria: running quick kpis from dashboards: p50 stable, p95 up, p99 worst. Prefill latency not huge per-request but prefill rate doubled; cache occupancy shows many small fragments (hot keys not contiguous). KV cache pressure graph: used_ratio=0.98, fragmentation_index=0.67.

sam: that fragmentation index is high. Looks like prefill paths are populating many small KV entries causing eviction of decoder-stage context (long-lived). So when decode happens we keep cold misses that require regen.

jess: hypothesis: prefill vs decode imbalance -> prefill churn populates the KV cache with ephemeral prefixes, evicting large decode-state entries (KV pages) used by active long streams. Result: tail requests pay the full decode again -> streaming stalls and tail latency up.

maria: confirmed via trace sampling: several p99 traces show hit_count on KV cache = 0 at decode start, then decode cost spikes (+700ms).

alex: urgent mitigations we can try (low risk first):
 - 1) rollback prefill heuristic flag on v2-serving (quick config flip)
 - 2) temporarily bump KV_CACHE_MEM_LIMIT for v2-serving pool by +20%
 - 3) enable eviction_bias to prefer removing small entries (prefer compact eviction)
 - 4) route high-prefill customers to fallback model without the prefill feature

sam: I'll take 2 and 3. prepping k8s patch to set env REDWOOD_KV_CACHE_MEM_LIMIT and eviction policy. will patch one AZ/pool at a time.

jess: I'll flip the prefill flag off on the rollout manager for v2-serving (can be done instantly).

maria: I'll coordinate with support to notify impacted customers with a short incident note: "We're investigating increased tail latency for streaming endpoints; mitigation in progress."

infra-bot: ACTIONABLE: creating rolling patch job for service=redwood-serving-v2 in cluster=prod-west. job id: job-7821.

sam: patch applied to pool-a workers (10%). mem limit +20% applied, eviction_bias=small_entries_first set. early signals: cache used_ratio dropped from 0.98 -> 0.82 in that shard set; fragmentation-index down 0.52. p95 trending down.

jess: prefill-heuristic flag flipped to off for v2-serving in rollout manager. traffic now handled with legacy prefill.

alex: quick A/B monitor: v2-serving pool with flag off shows p99 reduced to ~700ms in the sample. pools with flag on remain high.

maria: support update posted to customers: "We've applied mitigations to reduce tail latency; we're continuing to monitor and will follow up." :thumbsup:

sam: continuing rolling changes to remaining pools. will also schedule a graceful recycle of long-lived worker processes to clear fragmented KV allocations (staggered restarts).

jess: also enabling a short-term routing policy to spill ~15% of long-stream sessions to fallback-small-quant model (lower memory usage) while we stabilize. This should reduce new prefill pressure.

alex: monitoring: streaming stall rate down from 40% -> 11% over last 6m. p95 back to ~160ms, p99 at ~620ms. still above baseline but improving.

maria: root cause summary (draft): new prefill heuristic on v2-serving increases ephemeral KV insert rate -> high fragmentation and eviction of long-lived decoder KV entries -> decode stage cold misses -> tail latency spikes and streaming stalls.

sam: next steps (post-mitigation):
 - run cache-compaction routine to coalesce small entries (ops script queued)
 - add guardrail: limit prefill concurrent inserts per-session
 - add telemetry: per-shard fragmentation, per-request kv_hotness score
 - revert the prefill heuristic until we have quota/eviction protections in place

jess: I'll open a follow-up RFC for prefill design with perf constraints. assign to eng-runtime and eng-ml.

maria: incident severity: P1 -> downgraded to P2 as customer impact reduced and mitigations applied. logging final note and will create postmortem template.

support-pager: Customers notified. two customers asked for more details; assigned to solutions-eng for callbacks.

alex: marking incident as "mitigated" for now. leaving thread open for postmortem notes and schedule for compaction + RFC. Thanks all.

maria: assigning action items: sam - cache compaction script + schedule, jess - RFC, alex - postmortem draft, me - customer follow-ups. I'll do a handoff to the oncall for next shift at 17:50 UTC.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied, metrics improving.

sam: compaction script committed to infra repo: ```scripts/kv_compact.sh --shard-range=0-31 --max-rate=50/s``` will run overnight if approved.

jess: RFC created: PR #1287 in eng-runtime (wip).

alex: postmortem draft created in docs/incidents (link internal): https://redwood.internal/pm/1755004821-postmortem (placeholder).

maria: handoff complete. oncall for next 12h: @sam. thanks everyone :heart: 

sam: taking handoff. I'll keep an eye and follow up with postmortem next 24h.

alex: resolved for now. closing thread in 30m unless new regressions.
